name: midnight-passport-workspace
//deploy:passport:manual: THE FALLBACK, not the deploy command. Two paths reach production now, and
this is the second of them.
`vercel --prod`, run from THIS directory, is the deploy command. The
Vercel project's Root Directory is examples/passport-demo with "Include
source files outside of the Root Directory" on, so the builder gets the
whole repository and builds it itself — see `build:passport:remote`
above and docs/demo/deployment.md. Nothing is built on a laptop and no
local artefact is uploaded.
`deploy:passport:manual` builds HERE and uploads the finished output
with `vercel deploy --prebuilt`. It is for the case where the builder
cannot produce the artefacts — the pinned release asset is gone, the
upstream parameter bucket is down — or where the tree being shipped is
not one any release describes.
Neither of them is the SANCTIONED path. https://midnightpassport.com is
deployed by .github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml, from a published GitHub
release, and only from a commit that is an ancestor of
origin/demo/pwa-demo. What either command here does NOT do is the point:
no typecheck, no unit tests, no PWA check, no end-to-end run, and no check
that what it uploads corresponds to any commit — both ship whatever is on
disk, uncommitted changes included.
THERE ARE NOW THREE COPIES OF THE VITE_* VALUES, and they must be changed
together: the ones inlined in this script, deploy-demo.yml's `env:` block
(the copy the sanctioned path ships), and the Vercel project's own
Environment Variables, which is the only copy a REMOTE build can see —
`vercel --prod` runs vite on a builder, where nothing this file says is in
scope. `vercel env ls` reads them back.
VITE_MIDNIGHT_PROVING_URL and VITE_SPONSOR_URL take a comma-separated,
ORDERED list since 2026/08/31, tried left to right per request. The 1AM
stagenet gateway is second and deliberately so; deploy-demo.yml carries the
measurement that decided the order. VITE_FUNDER_URL stays a single URL:
/register-alias and /fund-account exist nowhere but our balancer.
docs/demo/deployment.md is the whole procedure: cutting a release, the
three repository secrets, and rolling back with `vercel promote`.
The other deploy:* scripts are unchanged — only the Passport demo has
continuous deployment so far.
//lint: The whole tree at once. `eslint.config.js` at the root carries the rules,
the two tiers, and the reasons; nothing is configured per workspace.
It is NOT in CI yet, and that is deliberate rather than forgotten. The
first full run reported 841 findings, so a gate added today would go red
on every pull request for reasons that have nothing to do with the pull
request. The order is: land the config, drive the count down, then add
`experiments/` is out of scope — see the note in eslint.config.js.

scripts.build: npm run build --workspace passport-demo-backend && npm run build --workspace passport-demo && npm run build --workspace passport-profile-client
scripts.deploy:passport:manual: node scripts/fetch-zk-artefacts.mjs && VITE_MIDNIGHT_NETWORK_ID=stagenet VITE_MIDNIGHT_PROVING_URL=https://67-205-177-162.sslip.io/prover,https://api-stagenet.1am.xyz VITE_SPONSOR_URL=https://67-205-177-162.sslip.io/balancer,https://api-stagenet.1am.xyz VITE_FUNDER_URL=https://67-205-177-162.sslip.io/balancer VITE_RAFFLE_URL=https://raffle.midnightpassport.com npm run build --workspace passport-demo && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-demo && cd examples/passport-demo && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes && cd ../.. && node scripts/tag-release.mjs
scripts.deploy:raffle: VITE_PASSPORT_ORIGIN=https://midnightpassport.com npm run build --workspace examples/raffle-demo && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/raffle-demo && cd examples/raffle-demo && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:template: cd examples/passport-app-template && VITE_PASSPORT_ORIGIN=https://midnightpassport.com npm run build && cd ../.. && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-app-template && cd examples/passport-app-template && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:hub: npm run build --workspace passport-app-hub && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-app-hub && cd examples/passport-app-hub && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.deploy:docs: npm run build --workspace passport-docs && node scripts/build-vercel-output.mjs examples/passport-docs && cd examples/passport-docs && vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --yes
scripts.build:passport:remote: node scripts/fetch-zk-artefacts.mjs && node examples/passport-demo/scripts/fetch-zk-params.mjs && npm run build --workspace passport-demo-backend && npm run build --workspace passport-demo

//build:passport:remote: What a VERCEL BUILDER runs. `vercel --prod` from this directory is the
deploy command now; the builder's Root Directory is examples/passport-demo
and that workspace's `vercel-build` hands straight back here.
It is the same four steps deploy-demo.yml runs, in the same order, and it
exists because a fresh checkout cannot build: the demo stages ~97 MB of
prover keys and ZKIR from examples/passport-balancer/contracts-stagenet
that is gitignored, plus ~45 MB of SRS slices from an upstream bucket.
The keys are downloaded, never compiled, and that IS a builder limitation
— which is a correction, dated 2026/09/10. This note used to say the
artefacts could not be compiled at all: the manifests named compactc
0.33.0-rc.2, which exists in midnightntwrk/compact for no platform (the
published set goes 0.31.1 then 0.34.0), and a different compiler was taken
to be a different verifier key. Measured, it is not. compactc 0.34.0
rebuilds all 23 of these verifier keys bit-identically to the ones the
stagenet contracts were deployed with, across the language bump to 0.26 it
requires and the runtime bump to 0.19.0. The builder simply has no
`compact` on PATH, and a 97 MB compile in front of every build would buy
nothing over a sha256 pin. `scripts/fetch-zk-artefacts.mjs` pins the bundle
by sha256 and then verifies every file in it against the tracked
`compiler/contract-manifest.json`, which is also what midnight-js checks at
run time before it will prove anything.
`npm ci` is NOT here: it is the builder's install step, run at this root
(see examples/passport-demo/vercel.json). The gates are not here either —
typecheck, tests, PWA checks, and the end-to-end run stay in
verify-demo.yml and deploy-demo.yml, where a failure blocks a release.
//dependencies: These are pinned HERE so that npm's hoisting is a decision rather than an
accident, and they are the LEDGER-9 versions. Nothing at the root imports
them: this list exists to decide WHICH COPY sits at the top of the tree.
Two Midnight stacks live in this workspace (see //overrides below), and
npm resolves that by hoisting one version of each name to the root and
nesting the other. Left to itself it hoisted the LEDGER-8 set, because
examples/passport-funder declares it — and then every ledger-9 package
that is only reachable transitively got hoisted beside it and nested its
OWN copy of the ledger-9 dependency it needed. That produces same-version
duplicates: midnight-js-protocol@5.0.0-beta.6 carrying a second physical
copy of compact-js@2.5.5-rc.7 while the demo used another. Two copies of
compact-js are two `CompactContext` TypeId symbols, and deployContract
dies with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ctor')` —
measured against stagenet, 2026/08/24, in the end-to-end drill.
So the root is the coherent LEDGER-9 side, and examples/passport-funder
nests its complete ledger-8 set beneath itself; it already declares every
one of these names explicitly, which is what makes that work. Keep this
list and examples/passport-demo's dependencies at the SAME versions — they
are the same stack, named twice for the resolver's benefit.
Why it has to be decided at all: a generated Compact contract module opens
with `import * as __compactRuntime from '@midnight-ntwrk/compact-runtime'`
and then `__compactRuntime.checkRuntimeVersion('<exact version>')`. Both
the bundler and Node resolve that specifier from the MODULE's directory,
walking upwards — so which copy a contract gets is decided by where the
contract file sits, not by which workspace asked for it. On top of that,
midnight-js decodes contract state through `ChargedState`, and two copies
of the runtime are two `ChargedState` classes: an `instanceof` check then
fails on objects that are correct in every other respect.
So both stacks are made coherent from opposite ends. The root holds the
ledger-9 runtime, which is what `examples/passport-demo` and the ledger-9
midnight-js packages hoisted alongside it all share — ONE copy, including
the contract modules staged into `examples/passport-demo/contracts/
stagenet`. `examples/passport-funder` names 0.16.0 in its own dependencies,
so it gets a nested copy that its bundle resolves first at run time; that
is the version the ledger-8 contract build it loads demands.
//overrides: Two Midnight stacks live in this workspace at once and must both resolve.
examples/passport-demo is on ledger-9 (wallet-sdk 2.0.0-beta.2, midnight-js
5.0.0-beta.7) for stagenet; examples/passport-funder stays on ledger-8
(wallet-sdk-* v3/v4, midnight-js 4.0.4) because preview is where it runs.
Every conflicting package is pinned to an exact version on both sides, so
npm nests the loser under the workspace that asks for it rather than
hoisting one over the other — npm gives the beta meta-package its whole
ledger-9 tree under node_modules/@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk/node_modules,
and leaves the ledger-8 copies of the same names at the root.
The one override below exists because @midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk
2.0.0-beta.2 pins wallet-sdk-utilities 1.2.0, a publish that does not
export `Clock`. wallet-sdk-facade imports `Clock`, so the whole wallet dies
— at build time, as the rollup error 'Clock is not exported by
…/wallet-sdk-utilities/dist/index.js'. 1.2.1 is the fixed publish.
It is written GLOBALLY, which is the blunt form, because the two surgical
forms were tried against this tree and neither reaches the copy that
matters. `"…-utilities@1.2.0": "1.2.1"` (by requested version) and
`{"@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk": {"@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk-utilities":
"1.2.1"}}` (scoped to the parent) both leave 1.2.0 sitting inside
node_modules/@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk/node_modules — which is exactly
where the beta tree lives, and where the broken copy is.
So it moves the funder's copy too, from 1.1.1 to 1.2.1, and that is
checked rather than assumed: passport-funder typechecks and builds clean
afterwards. Two packages in its own tree were already resolving 1.2.1
before this change, so it was never running 1.1.1 throughout.

reaches nothing but the funder's own tree, and 8.0.3 is the version the

Unlike the two overrides beside it this one is written BY REQUESTED
VERSION rather than globally, and the difference is measured: the global
form drags examples/passport-funder from 0.16.0 to 0.19.0 as well — an
override beats a workspace's own explicit pin — and `npm ls` then reports
for by nothing on the ledger-8 side, so naming it leaves the funder alone.
Added 2026/09/10 with the move to compactc 0.34.0. Without 0.19.0 a callee
in a contract-to-contract call shares the root contract's Zswap local
state (LFDT-Minokawa/compact#658); 0.19.0 keeps one per contract in the
call tree, which is what the one-transaction Passport transfer needs.
